reckon/crew/recovery.py:7926 (classify_pointer names a stranded launch in the launch-failed family)

findings.text: follow-on: _stranded_launch returns False when the pointer carries no attempt clock -- no attempt_started_at and no attempt.json -- so a stranded pointer that also lacks the clock is still left in flight; the observed incident's pointer carried attempt_started_at, but a pointer predating the field with no attempt record repeats the original symptom with the fix present.

follow-on: the release case asserts the standing claim no longer reads in flight and that composition proceeds, but never asserts a review was actually dispatched; the done-when asks the test to assert both the release and the redispatch, and the case's own comment concedes it measures only that the refusal is reached.

follow-on: the manifest's failure_attribution records all three head-arm failures as a read-only crew home (OSError Errno 30), but only test_cli_follow_streams_each_event_as_one_json_document fails that way; the two ticker tests fail on an extra trailing line 'reckon crew watch stopped: watch stream ended' corrupting their line-count and JSON assertions, and the Errno 30 in head.log is an unrelated obligation-sweep thread warning -- the ids match at base so the count is unaffected, but the stated cause would misdirect a later repair.

follow-on: the base arm was scoped to the three head failure ids rather than the full 62-file set (a deviation the manifest declares), so a failure the full base set would have shown elsewhere is not excluded.
